facts.raw_span: a three-week history of a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump
a low-grade fever (37.5–38°C) for one week
hypertension—treated with lacidipine, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide
a laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass performed two years earlier
lost 112 kg (BMI from 64.6 to 28 kg/m2)
smoked 30 cigarettes daily
took vitamin (A, D, E, B complex), calcium, cholecalciferol, and iron supplements
a tender, non-mobile, 3 × 4 cm lymph node in the left axilla

laboratory studies—including a complete blood count, ESR, liver and renal panels, autoantibodies (ANA, RF), complement levels, inflammatory markers, thyroid function, and serologies for a broad spectrum of viral and parasitic pathogens—were all normal or negative
thoracoabdominal CT scan was unremarkable except for the axillary lymphadenopathy
biopsy of the axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate
investigation for mycobacteria was negative

concepts.why: The patient presents with a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump and a low-grade fever, which are consistent with cat-scratch disease.
The patient's biopsy of the axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, which are characteristic of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
The patient presents with a tender, non-mobile lymph node in the left axilla, which is consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease.
The patient's biopsy of the axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, which may be indicative of lymphoma.
The patient presents with a tender, non-mobile lymph node in the left axilla, which is consistent with Castleman disease.

The patient presents with a tender, slow-growing left axillary lump and a low-grade fever, which are consistent with tuberculous lymphadenitis, although the investigation for mycobacteria was negative.
The patient presents with a tender, non-mobile lymph node in the left axilla, which is consistent with sarcoidosis.
The patient's biopsy of the axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate, which may be indicative of Kimura disease.

rationales.F01: The presence of a tender, slow-growing axillary lump is more typical of Cat-scratch disease and Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
rationales.F02: Low-grade fever is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in various conditions, including infections and autoimmune diseases.
rationales.F08: The presence of a tender, non-mobile lymph node in the axilla is more typical of Cat-scratch disease and Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
rationales.F11: The biopsy findings of coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate are more typical of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease.
rationales.F12: The negative investigation for mycobacteria rules out Tuberculous lymphadenitis.
